brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Four hex base pieces (piece:0,0,0 full; 0,1,0 full; 1,0,0 full; 1,-1,0 half-n) locked with two joint bolts. Two removable bins sit in the base cells: bin:0,0,0 (full depth, 2 compartments) and bin:0,1,0 (full depth, single well). Bins drop in and hang on their rims.
drawer:0#1,-1#cut (classic-style drawer 's') on the cut face of the half-n base piece:1,-1,0.
handle:1,0,0;top on the top cover cover:1,0,0;full;top, with its inserts. The configurator accepted it and check_build reports meshClash clear.
Compact build of about 14 parts with a handle on top. The configurator does not verify weight, strength or material; the print material choice is not checked here.

finish.summary: Built a small hex-base organizer: four base pieces with two removable bins, one drawer on a half base, and a top carry handle over a cover. check_build is clean (meshClash clear, no errors; only an informational cap-face note). Cosmetic note: the bins are not otherwise loaded with props, and the build has no lid or cover on most faces, which the brief did not require.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
